question: On a plain KUB X-ray, calcium-containing renal calculi appear radio-opaque and are visible, whereas uric acid stones are radiolucent and will not be seen on a plain film.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Radio-opacity on KUB depends on mineral composition: calcium-containing stones (commonest in children) are radio-opaque; uric acid stones are radiolucent. When KUB shows a pelvic or paraspinal density along the ureteric course, calculus must be considered.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate stones are radio-opaque (>90% of renal stones in children) and cast a radiodense shadow on KUB. Uric acid and cystine stones are radiolucent on plain film and require ultrasound or CT for detection.
